messages:
joon_customer: Hey team — our in-product chat stream goes silent in Safari after ~30s. EventSource connection drops and then client reconnects and we see duplicate partial messages. Repro on Safari 16.4. CDN shows 304 on the stream request. Headers below.

alex_support: Thanks — sorry about that. Can you paste the request/response headers + minimal repro steps? Also confirm if you're using a polyfill (event-source-polyfill) or a SW.

joon_customer: Repro steps: open chat, start streaming reply, wait ~30s.
Request (from browser devtools):
```
GET /v1/stream?session=abcd HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED
Origin: https://app.acme.com
Accept: text/event-stream
If-None-Match: "etag-123"
```
Response (intermittent): 304 Not Modified, then stream stops emitting new data until reconnect.

alex_support: Hmm — Safari + CF/CDN + SSE is tricky. Do you run a service worker or an eventsource polyfill? Safari sometimes treats a 304 differently and stops reading the connection body when caching is involved.

joon_customer: We're using `event-source-polyfill` and Cloudflare with standard caching rules. We do have an edge rule that strips query strings for certain paths (maybe relevant).

mike_network: FYI our infra telemetry has seen CDN responses with 304 for SSE endpoints when ETag is present and Authorization isn't part of Vary. If the edge caches a 304, the browser can end up with a half-closed stream. Try sending headers to avoid cache: `Cache-Control: no-store` or ensure `Vary: Authorization`.

sara_engineering: Can you run a raw curl to see behavior server-side? Example:
```
curl -v -H "Accept: text/event-stream" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?session=abcd"
```
Also check whether the server sends `Connection: keep-alive` and does not send `Content-Length` for streaming responses.

deploybot: Canary rollout cedar/streaming-opt at 2023-11-10T04:12:00Z — note: introduced gzip chunk coalescing on the runtime.

olivia_devex: Short mitigation you can try while we triage: 1) Add `Cache-Control: no-cache, no-transform` on request and response; 2) Remove ETag/If-None-Match for stream endpoints; 3) Ensure SSE includes per-event `id:` to handle dupes on reconnect.
Client-side polyfill note: force `fetch`-based polyfill to set `mode: 'cors'` and add `cache: 'no-store'` in the request so upstream CDN doesn't serve 304.

joon_customer: I flipped the CDN rule to bypass cache for /v1/stream and this fixed the chunk-truncation/partial outputs. Safari still reconnects after ~30s and sometimes the client gets duplicated events on reconnect.

sara_engineering: For duplicates, server should emit `id:` on each SSE event and the client should replay from `Last-Event-ID` — dedupe by id on server or client. We'll also audit the runtime's gzip coalescing to ensure chunks are flushed frequently.

alex_support: Escalating to eng-runtime + eng-sre to update CDN rules (add Vary: Authorization and bypass for streams) and push header changes: recommended response headers below.
```
Cache-Control: no-store, must-revalidate
Vary: Authorization, Origin
Connection: keep-alive
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
Content-Type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8
```

mike_network: Also check that intermediate proxies (CF workers) don't eagerly return 304 for streaming endpoints — set origin to return 200 with `Cache-Control: private, max-age=0` if needed.

joon_customer: Thanks — patch looks promising. Will monitor after the CDN change and report back. Appreciate the help :clap:

alex_support: Thanks, keeping this open until you confirm stability. If you can attach a HAR or network logs when it happens that helps us pin exact headers/timing.
